messages.content:
" *

Gets the class name minus the package name from a Class.

* * @param cls the class to get the short name for. * @return the class name without the package name or an empty string "

The `ClassUtils.getShortClassName(Class<?> cls)` method in the `org.apache.commons.lang` package is used to get the class name minus the package name from a Class object. It returns the class name without the package name or an empty string if the input Class object is null.

The current bug report describes that `ClassUtils.getShortClassName()` is not working correctly with arrays and seems to add a semicolon to the end of the class name for all arrays. The test case that failed is checking the short class name for an array of strings, expecting "String[]" but getting "String;" instead.

Based on the code snippet of `getShortClassName(Class<?> cls)`, it seems that this method simply calls `getShortClassName(String)` with the name of the input Class object. This behavior does not account for arrays correctly, resulting in the issue described in the bug report.

To fix this issue, we should modify the `getShortClassName(Class<?> cls)` method to handle arrays correctly by checking if the class is an array and formatting the class name appropriately.

Next, I will provide the methods that need to be fixed to address this bug.
`org.apache.commons.lang.ClassUtils.getShortClassName(java.lang.Class<?>)`

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
